tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting up a biological nutrient removal train in spring after a winter shutdown.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one BNR train returning to service at a large western Canadian plant, other trains remain in service.

cards.label: Start internal recycle and return sludge flows at low rates and confirm distribution
Sample ammonia, nitrate, and phosphate along the train daily as biomass establishes
Set the initial aerobic, anoxic, and anaerobic zone lineup for the spring nutrient targets
Raise loading in steps to the normal share once effluent nutrients are stable
Fill the train gradually and seed it with mixed liquor from an operating train
Review winter shutdown records and confirm all zone mixers, gates, and instruments are returned to service

tasks.explanation: Seeding and zone setup come before loading, recycle flows are proven at low rates first, and loading rises only after nutrient profiles show the biomass is established.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for commissioning an anoxic zone for denitrification in an existing aeration train.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one aeration train converted to include a dedicated anoxic zone, mixers installed, air headers valved off in that zone.

cards.label: Review influent carbon and nitrate loads to confirm the zone size can denitrify as designed
Bring the zone online at low internal recycle and confirm mixing without aeration
Confirm mixers run, air is isolated from the zone, and dissolved oxygen probes read correctly
Measure dissolved oxygen and oxidation reduction potential to confirm anoxic conditions hold
Increase internal recycle in steps to the design rate and record the final settings
Sample nitrate entering and leaving the zone to confirm removal is occurring

tasks.explanation: Equipment and load checks come before the zone goes live, anoxic conditions are proven before removal is claimed, and recycle rises in steps to the design rate.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for setting swing zone operation between aerobic and anoxic service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: swing zone can run aerated or mixed only, seasonal nutrient targets change next week.

cards.label: Confirm the effluent response and lock the zone in the new service until the next review
Agree the change date and target condition with the senior operator and record it in the plan
Review effluent ammonia and nitrate trends to decide which service the swing zone is needed in
Adjust wasting and aeration elsewhere in the train to prepare for the change
Sample ammonia and nitrate above and below the zone through the first day after the switch
Switch the zone by stopping air and starting mixers, or the reverse, in one controlled change

tasks.explanation: Trends decide the service before anything is switched, the plant is prepared before the change, and sampling proves the new service is working before it is locked in.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a biological nutrient removal profile sampling day along a treatment train.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: samples at the anaerobic, anoxic, aerobic, and effluent points of one BNR train on a normal loading day.

cards.label: Collect samples in flow order from the head of the train to the effluent point
Flag any zone that is off pattern and raise the follow up check in the process log
Plot ammonia, nitrate, and phosphate against train position and compare with the expected pattern
Record flows, recycle rates, and dissolved oxygen setpoints at the start of the sampling round
Calibrate field meters and prepare labelled bottles for ammonia, nitrate, phosphate, and dissolved oxygen
Measure dissolved oxygen and temperature at each point at the time of sampling

tasks.explanation: Meters and operating records frame the round before sampling starts, samples follow the flow path, and the plotted profile is what turns results into a zone diagnosis.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for returning a biological nutrient removal train to service after clarifier maintenance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: train was drained for secondary clarifier drive repair, repair is complete and tested dry.

cards.label: Inspect the clarifier and train, remove tools and lockouts, and confirm the drive runs freely
Refill the train with settled sewage and mixed liquor from operating trains
Restart return sludge and internal recycle at low rates and check for leaks and uneven flow
Increase the train share of influent flow in steps over several shifts
Sample effluent nutrients daily until the train matches the other trains and record the return
Restore the zone aeration and mixing pattern used before the outage

tasks.explanation: The train is proven mechanically before it is refilled, flows restart low and rise in steps, and nutrient sampling confirms full return to service.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for establishing an internal mixed liquor recycle rate program for denitrification.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: internal recycle pumps return nitrate rich mixed liquor from the aerobic zone to the anoxic zone.

cards.label: Record the final ratio, pump settings, and nitrate results in the nutrient control plan
Adjust the ratio in small steps, allowing a full day between changes
Sample nitrate at the anoxic zone outlet daily to confirm it is near the target low value
Select the starting recycle ratio that matches the anoxic zone carbon and capacity
Calculate the nitrate load reaching the end of the aerobic zone from recent profiles
Set the recycle pumps to the starting ratio and verify actual flow at the meter

tasks.explanation: The nitrate load sets the starting ratio, actual flow is verified before results are judged, and small daily steps prevent chasing noise in the data.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for setting a step feed distribution program for a biological nutrient removal plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: influent can be split between the head of the train and a downstream feed point, wet season is approaching.

cards.label: Brief all shifts on the new split, the gate positions, and the checks required
Keep, adjust, or reverse the split at the weekly review based on the recorded results
Move the feed gates to the new split in one change during a stable loading period
Calculate the feed split that reserves enough carbon for denitrification without overloading the clarifier
Monitor nitrate, ammonia, and blanket depth daily through the first week
Review carbon, ammonia, and clarifier loading data for the current single point feed pattern

tasks.explanation: Data and calculation come before gates move, crews are briefed before the change, and a week of monitoring decides whether the split stays.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for setting up oxidation reduction potential based control checks for nutrient removal zones.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: ORP probes in the anaerobic, anoxic, and aerobic zones, plant wants trend based zone checks.

cards.label: Record baseline ORP ranges in each zone during a week of good nutrient performance
Review the bands monthly and revise them when profile data shows they have drifted
Clean and calibrate the ORP probes and verify them against a standard solution
Compare the baselines with dissolved oxygen and nutrient profile results from the same week
Set the working ORP bands for each zone in the nutrient control plan
Use the bands as a daily screening check alongside, not instead of, nutrient sampling

tasks.explanation: Baselines must come from proven good performance before bands are set, ORP screens daily operation, and nutrient profiles remain the confirming evidence.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a foam and filament control program on a biological nutrient removal train.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: stable brown foam and rising filament levels on one BNR train, effluent quality is still in range.

cards.label: Check the anaerobic and anoxic selectors for short circuiting or oxygen intrusion
Repeat microscopy weekly and record whether foam and filaments are receding
Waste surface foam to solids handling rather than returning it to the train
Apply the matched control, such as a retention time change or selector repair, in one step
Examine mixed liquor and foam microscopically to identify the dominant filament type
Review solids retention time, dissolved oxygen, and nutrient balance records for the train

tasks.explanation: Identification comes before control selection, selector faults are ruled out before chemical or wasting changes, and repeat microscopy proves whether the program works.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for taking one biological nutrient removal train out of service while protecting nutrient limits.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one of three BNR trains needs a two week outage, provincial wastewater requirements and federal effluent limits still apply.

cards.label: Drain and isolate the outage train and transfer its mixed liquor to the operating trains
Calculate the loading the remaining trains must carry and confirm it is within their nutrient capacity
Brief all shifts on the outage loading pattern, sampling frequency, and escalation triggers
Raise solids inventory gradually in the remaining trains before the outage starts
Sample effluent ammonia, total nitrogen, and phosphorus daily through the outage
Return the train in steps after the work and rebalance flows once nutrients are stable

tasks.explanation: Capacity is proven and inventory is built before the train is drained, daily nutrient sampling guards the outage, and return follows the same stepped pattern.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a winter solids handling and site safety program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: cake hauling, dewatering, and outdoor solids work continue through deep winter.

cards.label: Check that dewatering, polymer, and cake handling equipment start reliably in the cold
Brief crews on cold exposure limits, warm up breaks, and ice reporting
Review winter incidents and near misses at spring thaw and update the program
Track stored cake volume weekly and trigger hauling before storage is full
Confirm outdoor lighting, walkways, and loading areas are cleared and treated for ice
Review the winter hauling schedule and storage trigger levels with the hauler

tasks.explanation: Hauling and storage are agreed before winter, equipment cold starts are proven, and weekly volume tracking prevents a storage emergency in deep cold.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for putting a biological nutrient removal plant into wet weather mode.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: forecast shows a major melt and rain event, influent flow will rise well above average for two days.

cards.label: Sample effluent nutrients and solids more often through the event and log any excursion
Protect biomass by holding wasting steady and keeping anoxic zones mixed during the peak
Raise return sludge rates and confirm clarifier drives and scrapers are ready for high loading
Review the forecast, current solids inventory, clarifier blankets, and available tank volume
Return to normal settings in steps as flow recedes and confirm inventory is recovered
Adjust the feed split and recycle rates to the wet weather settings in the operations plan

tasks.explanation: Readiness and inventory checks come before settings change, biomass is protected through the peak, and normal operation resumes in steps as flow falls.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for operating a biological nutrient removal plant in low load holiday mode.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: industrial contributors shut down for a week, influent load falls to about half of normal.

cards.label: Restore normal aeration and train lineup in steps as contributor flows restart
Confirm the load drop with influent flow and biochemical oxygen demand results
Watch carbon availability for denitrification and phosphorus removal as loads fall
Hold wasting changes small so inventory is ready when normal load returns
Reduce aeration output to hold dissolved oxygen targets without over aerating the low biomass load
Consider resting one train or zone if inventory can be held safely in fewer trains

tasks.explanation: The load drop is confirmed before aeration is cut, nutrient removal carbon is watched while loads are low, and restart is stepped so the plant meets the returning load.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for coordinating return sludge control between biological nutrient removal and the secondary clarifiers.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: return sludge affects both clarifier blankets and denitrification, senior operator is setting a joint routine.

cards.label: Record the band and the recheck results in the joint clarifier and nutrient routine
Profile blanket depth and return sludge concentration in each clarifier on the same round
Recheck blankets and anoxic nitrate after one clarifier turnover time
Review anoxic zone nitrate results to see how much nitrate the return flow is carrying back
Set a return rate band that holds blankets in range without flooding the anoxic zone with nitrate
Adjust return rates into the band in one step per clarifier

tasks.explanation: Blankets and nitrate are measured together because one return rate serves both, the band balances the two needs, and the recheck proves the compromise works.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for establishing an alkalinity monitoring program for a nitrifying biological nutrient removal plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plant nitrifies year round, influent alkalinity varies with melt water, no routine alkalinity testing exists yet.

cards.label: Set the sampling frequency and the low alkalinity action level in the control plan
Add the program to the weekly process review with results trended beside ammonia
Run the first month of sampling and compare alkalinity consumed with ammonia removed
Select sampling points at the influent, aerobic zone outlet, and final effluent
Review past ammonia, pH, and any alkalinity results to find when the plant ran lowest
Confirm whether natural alkalinity is sufficient or a supplementation trial is needed

tasks.explanation: History shows when risk is highest before points and levels are set, a month of paired data proves consumption, and trending keeps the program alive after setup.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for an annual biological nutrient removal performance review at a large plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: senior team reviews a full year of nutrient, energy, and chemical data before setting next year targets.

cards.label: Issue the review summary and file it with the annual operations report
Calculate removal performance and chemical and energy use per unit of nutrient removed
Agree target ranges, projects, and trials for the coming year with owners assigned
Compare the year with provincial requirements and the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations limits
Identify the months and events where performance fell short and the conditions behind them
Compile monthly influent and effluent nitrogen and phosphorus loads for the full year

tasks.explanation: Loads and unit costs are compiled before shortfalls are judged, compliance is checked against both levels of requirements, and agreed targets close the review.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for recovering nitrification after an effluent ammonia breakthrough.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: effluent ammonia has risen above the plant action level for two days at a western Canadian BNR plant.

cards.label: Check wastewater temperature, dissolved oxygen, pH, and alkalinity for a limiting condition
Confirm the breakthrough with a repeat effluent sample and check the online ammonia trend
Check for a toxic or high load discharge in the influent records and notify the senior operator
Sample effluent ammonia daily and restore normal wasting only after results are back in range
Raise aerobic zone dissolved oxygen into the nitrification band if oxygen is limiting
Reduce wasting at once to protect and rebuild the nitrifier population

tasks.explanation: Confirmation and limiting factor checks come before wasting is cut, nitrifiers are protected while the cause is fixed, and daily sampling proves recovery.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting external carbon dosing to improve denitrification.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: effluent nitrate is high, influent carbon is short, a carbon product and dosing pump are available.

cards.label: Set up the dosing pump, verify its output by drawdown, and confirm storage and safety checks
Sample anoxic outlet nitrate and effluent biochemical oxygen demand daily for the first week
Confirm carbon shortage with influent carbon to nitrogen data and anoxic zone nitrate profiles
Calculate the starting carbon dose from the nitrate mass to be removed using the product factor
Raise the dose in steps to the full rate only if nitrate falls without effluent carbon rising
Start dosing at half the calculated rate to the head of the anoxic zone

tasks.explanation: Shortage is proven before product is bought into service, the pump is verified before dosing starts low, and effluent carbon guards against overdosing.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for setting a chemical phosphorus removal trim program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: biological phosphorus removal meets the target most days, chemical trim is needed for high load days.

cards.label: Run jar tests on effluent to select the chemical and the dose range for the trim
Adjust the dose pacing so the target is met without large chemical carryover to the effluent
Set the dosing point, pump range, and the flow paced control settings
Review effluent phosphorus data to find the load pattern on days the target is missed
Record the trigger conditions and doses so any shift can start the trim the same way
Start trim dosing on the next high load day and sample phosphorus above and below the dose point

tasks.explanation: Missed days define when trim is needed, jar tests set the dose before pumps run, and recorded triggers make the program repeatable across shifts.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for troubleshooting poor biological phosphorus removal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: effluent phosphorus has risen over two weeks, anaerobic zone is in service, chemical trim is available.

cards.label: Check wasting and retention time for a change that favours competing organisms over phosphorus accumulators
Correct the single most likely cause and hold other settings steady
Profile phosphate again after several days and confirm release and uptake have recovered
Check the anaerobic zone for nitrate or dissolved oxygen intrusion from recycle flows
Review influent volatile fatty acid and carbon data for a drop in fermentable load
Profile phosphate along the train to confirm whether release in the anaerobic zone has weakened

tasks.explanation: The profile locates the failure before causes are chased, intrusion and carbon are checked before biology is blamed, and a second profile proves the fix.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting an alkalinity supplementation program for nitrification.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: effluent alkalinity is low, pH in the aerobic zone is falling, ammonia removal is at risk.

cards.label: Select the feed point and verify the chemical system output by a drawdown test
Sample effluent alkalinity and ammonia daily through the first two weeks
Compare consumption with influent alkalinity to size the daily supplementation need
Start feeding at the calculated rate and monitor aerobic zone pH twice per shift
Settle the feed rate into the control plan with low alkalinity alarm actions recorded
Calculate alkalinity consumed from the ammonia mass nitrified using the factor in the control plan

tasks.explanation: Consumption is calculated before a rate is chosen, the feed system is verified before it runs, and pH plus alkalinity sampling proves the program holds.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a monthly total nitrogen optimization review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: senior operator reviews nitrogen data monthly to tune denitrification at a BNR plant.

cards.label: Identify the one setting change most likely to improve total nitrogen next month
Compile influent and effluent nitrogen species and loads for the month
Compare performance with internal recycle, carbon dose, and dissolved oxygen settings in use
Calculate ammonia, nitrate, and total nitrogen removal for each week of the month
Review the flagged change at the next monthly review before making another
Apply the change at the start of the month and flag it in the trend charts

tasks.explanation: Loads and removal are calculated before settings are compared, one change at a time keeps cause and effect clear, and the next review judges that change.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a monthly total phosphorus optimization review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plant uses biological removal with chemical trim, phosphorus data is reviewed monthly.

cards.label: Apply the adjustment and increase effluent phosphorus sampling for the first two weeks
Report the trial outcome and the chemical cost per unit removed at the next review
Compile influent, effluent, and waste sludge phosphorus loads for the month
Review anaerobic zone profiles and chemical doses used on missed target days
Select one biological or chemical adjustment to trial for the next month
Separate biological removal performance from chemical trim performance in the data

tasks.explanation: Biological and chemical removal are separated before either is adjusted, the trial is sampled more closely at first, and cost per unit removed judges its value.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for implementing ammonia based aeration control on an aerobic zone.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: aerobic zone has an online ammonia analyser, blowers can be paced by the control system.

cards.label: Program the ammonia setpoint and the dissolved oxygen high and low limits with senior approval
Record dissolved oxygen and ammonia patterns under manual control to set the control bands
Verify the ammonia analyser against laboratory samples over several days of varied loading
Switch to automatic control during a stable loading period with alarms set
Review energy use and effluent ammonia weekly and tune the bands only on that evidence
Run the control in monitoring mode first, comparing its calls with operator judgement

tasks.explanation: The analyser is proven before it controls anything, monitoring mode tests the logic safely, and weekly evidence governs any tuning after go live.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a nitrate recycle optimization trial.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: trial will test two internal recycle ratios for two weeks each on one BNR train.

cards.label: Sample anoxic and effluent nitrate daily through the first trial period
Select the better ratio, set it as the standard, and file the trial summary
Set the first trial ratio and hold all other nutrient settings steady
Compare total nitrogen, effluent quality, and pumping energy between the two periods
Set the second trial ratio and repeat the same daily sampling
Record baseline nitrate, total nitrogen, and energy data at the current recycle ratio

tasks.explanation: Baseline data comes first, only the ratio changes between periods so the comparison is fair, and selection follows the measured trade off.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for investigating secondary phosphorus release in a secondary clarifier.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: effluent phosphorus is higher than aerobic zone outlet phosphorus, blankets have been deep.

cards.label: Check dissolved oxygen in the clarifier feed for conditions that trigger release
Record the return rate that holds release in check in the clarifier routine
Raise return sludge rate in one step to shorten solids holding time in the clarifier
Resample phosphorus at the same points after one day at the new return rate
Sample phosphorus at the aerobic outlet, clarifier effluent, and return sludge on the same round
Profile blanket depth and estimate how long solids are held in the clarifier

tasks.explanation: Paired sampling proves release is happening in the clarifier before return rates change, holding time is the lever, and resampling confirms the correction.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for responding to a nutrient spike from a hauled waste or industrial discharge.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: influent ammonia and organic load spike after a hauled waste delivery at a large plant.

cards.label: Review the delivery acceptance procedure with the hauler before the next load is accepted
Sample effluent ammonia and nutrients every few hours until the spike passes
Notify the senior operator and log the event under the plant response procedure
Increase aeration and hold wasting to protect nitrifiers through the spike
Divert or equalize part of the load if tankage is available and approved for use
Confirm the spike with influent sampling and the hauled waste delivery records

tasks.explanation: Records confirm the source before the plant reacts, biomass and aeration are protected through the event, and acceptance rules are tightened before it can recur.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for operating a selector zone to control filamentous growth while protecting nutrient removal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: selector at the head of the BNR train, filaments rising, nutrient targets still apply.

cards.label: Adjust selector loading or oxygen in one step matched to the filament identified
Measure dissolved oxygen and load entering the selector to confirm it creates the intended condition
Check that return sludge and influent are mixing fully in the selector with no short circuit
Monitor settling, microscopy, and nutrient profiles together weekly
Record the selector settings that restored settling without harming nutrient removal
Confirm filament type and abundance by microscopic examination

tasks.explanation: Identification and selector condition checks come before adjustment, settling and nutrients are judged together, and the working settings are recorded for the next event.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for checking simultaneous nitrification and denitrification in a low dissolved oxygen basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: basin runs at low dissolved oxygen, effluent nitrate is lower than expected, senior operator wants proof of the mechanism.

cards.label: Profile ammonia, nitrate, and dissolved oxygen along the basin on the same round
Check floc and microscopy for conditions that support zones of low oxygen inside floc
Review blower output and probe locations to rule out a measurement artefact
Decide whether to keep the low oxygen strategy and record the evidence either way
Compare total nitrogen removal between the two profiles at similar loading
Hold the dissolved oxygen setpoint steady for a week and repeat the profile

tasks.explanation: Artefacts are ruled out before the mechanism is claimed, a steady week separates pattern from noise, and the decision rests on repeated profiles.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for transitioning to tighter seasonal nutrient targets in spring.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: provincial requirements set tighter nutrient expectations for the open water season, plant must be ready by the change date.

cards.label: Review the seasonal target dates and values in the plant approval and operations plan
Make the settings changes in steps during the two weeks before the change date
Confirm compliance at the first monthly review and record lessons for next year
Assess current nutrient margins and the settings changes needed to meet the tighter targets
Schedule inventory build, carbon supply, and chemical stock checks ahead of the date
Increase effluent nutrient sampling through the first month of the new season

tasks.explanation: Targets and margins are reviewed before changes are scheduled, settings move ahead of the date rather than on it, and the first month is sampled closely.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for completing a monthly nutrient mass balance for the whole plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: month end balance covers influent, effluent, waste sludge, and chemical phosphorus removal.

cards.label: Reconcile received mass against discharged, removed, and stored mass and investigate large gaps
File the balance with the monthly report and note any sampling gap that weakens it
Total nutrient mass removed in waste sludge and in chemical sludge during the month
Total effluent nitrogen and phosphorus mass discharged during the month
Account for inventory change in the trains and digesters over the month
Total influent nitrogen and phosphorus mass received during the month

tasks.explanation: All mass terms are totalled before reconciliation, gaps are investigated rather than averaged away, and sampling weaknesses are declared in the report.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for designing a solids retention time optimization study at a large BNR plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: study will test retention time against nitrification, phosphorus removal, settling, and energy over one season.

cards.label: Set the sampling program for ammonia, phosphorus, settling, and microscopy for each trial stage
Record baseline performance at the current retention time for at least two weeks
Move retention time to the first trial value by a calculated wasting change
Define the study question, the target outcomes, and the retention time range to be tested
Hold each trial value long enough for the biomass to reach the new condition before judging it
Compare stages on all outcomes together and recommend the optimum with the evidence attached

tasks.explanation: The question and baseline come before any wasting change, each stage is held long enough to be real, and the optimum is judged on all outcomes together.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for raising solids retention time for winter nitrification protection at a multi train plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: wastewater temperature is falling, all trains must carry a higher winter inventory.

cards.label: Reduce wasting in small steps over two to three weeks rather than in one change
Work out the wasting reduction for each train to build inventory evenly
Calculate the winter inventory needed from the temperature corrected nitrification target in the plan
Record the winter wasting rates and hold them until the spring review date
Sample effluent ammonia and mixed liquor daily through the build period
Confirm aeration and clarifier capacity can carry the higher inventory as it builds

tasks.explanation: The winter inventory is calculated before wasting changes, the build is gradual and even across trains, and capacity checks run alongside the build.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for lowering solids retention time in the spring transition at a multi train plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: wastewater has warmed, winter inventory is higher than summer operation needs.

cards.label: Watch settling, foam, and phosphorus removal as younger sludge develops
Confirm sustained warming and stable effluent ammonia at the current inventory
Sample effluent ammonia daily until the summer inventory is reached and stable
Increase wasting in steps, one train leading so its response can be read first
Calculate the summer inventory target and the wasting increase needed for each train
Record the summer wasting rates and the date the transition completed

tasks.explanation: Warming and ammonia stability are proven before inventory is shed, one train leads so surprises are contained, and daily ammonia sampling guards the transition.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running a daily solids retention time control program using waste sludge mass.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: daily program uses measured waste volume and concentration, not pump timers alone.

cards.label: Calculate the mass wasted in the previous day from measured volume and concentration
Calculate the solids inventory in the aeration trains and clarifiers
Compare the calculated retention time with the target band for the season
Adjust the waste pump setting by the calculated amount if the value is outside the band
Enter the day values on the retention time trend and hand the trend to the next shift
Sample mixed liquor and waste sludge and record the results for the day

tasks.explanation: Inventory and wasted mass must both be measured before retention time is known, adjustment follows the comparison, and the trend carries the story between shifts.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for correcting a solids retention time drift caused by unmeasured clarifier inventory.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: calculated retention time keeps rising even though wasting matches the plan, blankets are deep.

cards.label: Raise return rates in steps to move blanket solids back to the trains where they are measured
Profile blanket depth in every clarifier and estimate the solids held in the blankets
Revise the daily inventory method to include a blanket estimate from now on
Add the clarifier inventory to the aeration inventory and recalculate retention time
Recheck blanket profiles after the return change and confirm inventories have shifted
Record the correction and its size in the process log for the monthly review

tasks.explanation: The missing inventory is measured before the calculation is trusted again, return rates move the solids to where they count, and the method is fixed so the drift cannot hide again.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for adjusting solids retention time during a filamentous bulking episode.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sludge volume index is high, microscopy shows filamentous growth, effluent solids are rising.

cards.label: Decide whether the matched response is a retention time rise, fall, or no change, with senior approval
Make the wasting change in one calculated step toward the decided direction
Return wasting toward normal in steps once settling and effluent solids recover
Run settling tests and microscopy twice weekly through the episode
Identify the filament type and check dissolved oxygen, nutrients, and load for its growth cause
Hold other process settings steady so the retention time effect can be read clearly

tasks.explanation: Cause identification decides the direction before wasting moves, other settings are held so the effect is readable, and recovery is proven by settling tests before normal wasting resumes.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for balancing solids retention time between nitrifiers and phosphorus accumulating organisms.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: longer retention time helps nitrification but phosphorus removal has weakened at the current setting.

cards.label: Profile phosphate release and uptake to confirm the phosphorus side of the trade off
Set the balanced retention time band and record the trade off evidence in the plan
Check whether aeration, carbon, or chemical trim can relieve the phosphorus side first
Judge the trial on both nutrients together, not on either one alone
Trial a small retention time step and sample both ammonia and phosphorus daily
Review ammonia and phosphorus performance together over the last month at the current retention time

tasks.explanation: Both nutrients are reviewed together because the setting serves both, relief options are tried before the compromise moves, and the band records the balance found.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a foam control program that uses solids retention time to wash out foam forming organisms.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: persistent Nocardia type foam, plant can waste foam and adjust retention time within nutrient limits.

cards.label: Waste foam from the surface to solids handling and stop any foam return to the trains
Watch nitrification closely, since the washout range sits near the nitrifier limit
Hold the lower retention time until microscopy shows the organism is receding
Lower retention time in calculated steps toward the washout range for the organism
Raise retention time back into the nutrient band in steps once foam is controlled
Confirm the foam organism by microscopy and map foam coverage by train

tasks.explanation: Foam is removed physically while retention time works biologically, nitrification is the guardrail during washout, and the return to normal waits for microscopy proof.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running a single train solids retention time step test while other trains hold steady.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one train will trial a new retention time, two trains stay at the standard setting as controls.

cards.label: Sample nutrients, settling, and microscopy on the same schedule for every train
Record two weeks of baseline data on all trains at the standard setting
Keep flows, aeration strategy, and sampling identical across all trains during the test
Compare the trial train with the control trains at similar loading at the end of the test
Calculate and apply the wasting change that sets the trial train to the test retention time
Adopt, extend, or abandon the new setting based on the comparison and file the result

tasks.explanation: Controls only work if everything else stays identical, baselines precede the change, and adoption follows the side by side comparison.
